architectural_principle: Cross-capability communication is exclusively async events. Within a capability, services communicate freely.

services.description: Primary service for JRN-015. Owns the entire wealth review lifecycle: scheduling, suitability assessment, rebalancing recommendation, trade instruction, and post-review reporting. Wraps the custody platform (FNZ/SEI) as an internal external dependency.

consumed_events.name: KYCClearanceGranted
consumed_events.purpose: JRN-015 PH-071 start: SVC-016 checks KYC status is current before scheduling the review. Reuses EVT-004 from prior journeys (JRN-001/JRN-006 pattern). If KYC has lapsed, review scheduling is suspended until KYC is refreshed.

field_mappings.notes: Confirms KYC is current for this client_id before review is scheduled

consumed_events.name: ClientAccountSummaryProvided
consumed_events.purpose: JRN-015 ALT-002 (PH-073): Response to ClientAccountDataRequested (EVT-101). SVC-001 returns a point-in-time cash balance summary for the HNW client. SVC-016 uses this to populate the liquidity buffer in the RebalancingRecommendation.

field_mappings.notes: Point-in-time cash balance for liquidity buffer assessment
Logged for audit; not persisted on ENT-048

consumed_apis.call_pattern: Synchronous (blocking per order submission); async confirmation callback
consumed_apis.purpose: JRN-015 PH-075: Submit rebalancing trade orders to the custody platform. Receive trade confirmations and settlement notifications asynchronously. Internal dependency within CAP-006 — not a cross-capability call.
Dispatch client notifications: review meeting confirmation, suitability report ready, trade execution confirmation, post-review report available.
Client authentication for wealth portal sessions. Advisor SSO authentication via SM&CR identity verification.
Immutable audit log for all regulated advisor actions: suitability report issuance, trade instruction creation, client acknowledgement. COBS 9A 5-year retention.

design_decisions.decision: SVC-016 is a new service introduced by JRN-015. It is the sole service within CAP-006.
design_decisions.rationale: All CAP-006 sub-capabilities (investment advisory, portfolio management, private banking, financial planning) scored 0/4 on the promotion test. They are all RETAINED — implemented as internal modules within SVC-016, sharing the same database and deployment unit.

design_decisions.decision: Custody platform (FNZ/SEI) is modelled as an external integration within SVC-016, not as a separate service or capability.
design_decisions.rationale: Custody is a buy candidate (DD-002 in CAP-006). SVC-016 wraps the custody API. The custody platform does not appear as a capability or service in the architecture — it is a vendor integration within SVC-016's boundary.

consumed_events.name: SuitabilityReportIssued
consumed_events.purpose: JRN-015 PH-074: SVC-014 receives the suitability report issuance event and creates a lightweight SuitabilityRecord in its compliance store. This provides the CAP-005 compliance audit trail for MiFID II COBS 9A.

maps_to.entity: SuitabilityRecord (internal to SVC-014, CAP-005 — not a JRN-015 data model entity)

field_mappings.notes: Updated risk profile at time of review

consumed_events.name: ConsumerDutyEvidenceCompleted
consumed_events.purpose: JRN-015 PH-076: SVC-014 receives the Consumer Duty evidence completion event and appends a record to the Consumer Duty monitoring register (CAP-005 internal store). Used for FCA supervisory reporting and fair value assessment aggregation.

field_mappings.notes: Encrypted; used for portfolio-level fair value aggregation
Triggers compliance team alert if true

design_decisions.decision: SVC-014 consumes two new cross-capability events from SVC-016 for JRN-015: SuitabilityReportIssued (EVT-103) and ConsumerDutyEvidenceCompleted (EVT-106). No new entities are introduced in SVC-014 — the compliance records are internal data structures within CAP-005.
design_decisions.rationale: CAP-005 must maintain the authoritative compliance audit trail for all regulated activities across all capabilities. Receiving events rather than being called synchronously preserves the cross-capability async rule.

consumed_events.name: ClientAccountDataRequested
consumed_events.purpose: JRN-015 ALT-002 (PH-073): SVC-001 receives the account data request, assembles a minimal account summary (available balance, account type), and publishes ClientAccountSummaryProvided (EVT-107). This is the sole mechanism for SVC-016 to access CAP-001 account data.

field_mappings.notes: Filter to requested account types (savings, current)

design_decisions.decision: SVC-001 introduces a new published event EVT-107 (ClientAccountSummaryProvided) as a response to EVT-101 (ClientAccountDataRequested) from SVC-016. The event carries minimal data: available_balance_gbp, account_type, snapshot_at.
design_decisions.rationale: The wealth review requires only a point-in-time liquidity snapshot — not a full account history. The minimal event payload reduces PII exposure and avoids replicating account data in CAP-006.

cross_service_interaction_summary.rationale: MiFID II COBS 9A and Consumer Duty compliance records must be registered in CAP-005's central compliance audit trail. Async events preserve the capability boundary.
Holistic wealth review requires the client's retail banking cash balance for liquidity buffer assessment. Async event request-response is the only valid cross-capability data access pattern.
SVC-016 checks KYC status before scheduling the review. Reuses existing EVT-004 cross-capability event.
